title: Incident Review: KMS Rotation for session_tokens_v2 Caused MFA Prompts and Login Failures (2026-03-22)
author: Maya Hernandez
content:
h1. Summary
On 2026-03-22, a scheduled KMS rotation for the secret *session_tokens_v2* caused a widespread increase in SSO authentication failures, leading to repeated MFA prompts and some account lockouts. The incident was triggered when the alias for *session_tokens_v2* was moved to a new key before session tokens encrypted under the previous key were re-encrypted. A re-encryption job failed, and the automation then scheduled deletion of the prior key, reducing our ability to decrypt legacy sessions.

No evidence of account compromise or malicious activity was found. The observed anomalies were consistent with decryption errors.

h1. Customer Impact
* *User-facing symptoms*: login errors, repeated MFA prompts, intermittent SSO failures; some lockouts due to repeated failed attempts.
* *Affected surface area*: SSO flows backed by auth-service session token decryption.
* *Severity*: SEV-2 (widespread auth degradation with partial loss of function).
* *Duration*: ~10:02 UTC to ~10:48 UTC elevated error rates; residual elevated MFA prompts until re-encryption completed.
* *Measured impact*:
** Peak SSO auth_failure alerts: ~500+ failures / 12 minutes (baseline ~low single digits).
** Estimated impacted sign-in attempts: ~18% at peak; recovered to <1% after mitigations.
** Lockouts: 31 confirmed across tenants (auto-unlocked after policy window or manual support intervention).

h1. Detection
* Primary detection: Redwood monitoring alert *“SSO auth_failures spike (3σ)”* correlated with KMS rotate job *rot-2026-03-22-1000*.
* Supporting signals:
** auth-service log errors: *session_decrypt_failed* and increased MFA challenges.
** Audit log events: alias update followed by *ScheduleDelete* of the previous key.

h1. Timeline (UTC)
* *10:00* Rotation automation starts for secret *session_tokens_v2* (job rot-2026-03-22-1000).
* *10:01* Alias updated to point to new key (old-key-abc -> new-key-def).
* *10:02* Auth failures begin spiking; users observe MFA loops.
* *10:03* Automation schedules deletion of old key (old-key-abc) (deletion window was not immediate, but access path became unreliable due to alias move).
* *10:06* On-call incident declared; rotation automation paused.
* *10:12* Mitigation deployed (auth-service hotfix): temporary legacy decryption path using explicit key-id lookup / keyring.
* *10:18* Cancel pending key deletion executed successfully; old key retained.
* *10:24* Canary success improves materially; rollout proceeds.
* *10:35* Error rates drop below alert threshold; MFA prompts normalize.
* *11:20* Re-encryption job re-run with backoff + network retry fix.
* *12:05* Re-encryption completes (all active tenants), plus verification step confirms decrypt for both key generations.
* *12:30* Temporary auth-service fallback remains enabled pending full observation window.
* *2026-03-23* Fallback removed after 24h of stable metrics; incident closed.

h1. What Happened (Technical Details)
Session tokens are encrypted with a KMS key referenced by alias *session_tokens_v2*. The rotation workflow was intended to:
# create/activate new key
# re-encrypt existing session tokens (or ensure decrypt supports both)
# move alias to new key
# only then schedule deletion of the old key after a safe retention period

In this incident, the automation effectively performed:
# move alias first
# attempt re-encryption
# schedule deletion of old key

Because the alias moved, decrypt operations that depended on the alias no longer referenced the old key. The re-encryption task failed due to a transient network error to the KMS client during peak load, so many still-valid sessions remained encrypted under the old key. These sessions then failed decrypt in auth-service, driving the MFA/login fallout.

Representative auth log line:
{code}
ERROR: session_decrypt_failed: key_id=old-key-abc not found during decrypt for session_id=...
{code}

h1. Root Cause
*Primary root cause*: KMS rotation automation updated the *session_tokens_v2* alias before ensuring session tokens encrypted with the previous key were either (a) re-encrypted successfully or (b) decryptable via multi-key fallback.

*Contributing factors*:
* Re-encryption job did not have robust retry/backoff and failed on a transient network issue.
* Rotation automation included a *ScheduleDelete* step for the old key in the same run, increasing risk and shortening the recovery path.
* Missing automated smoke test immediately after alias change to validate decrypt of existing sessions.
* Incomplete guardrails: the job was permitted to move alias without a “re-encryption success” gate.

h1. Resolution and Recovery
Immediate mitigations:
* Paused rotation automation for all session-related secrets.
* Cancelled pending deletion for old key (old-key-abc) and set an explicit retention window.
* Deployed auth-service hotfix to allow decryption using explicit key IDs / keyring lookup for legacy sessions until re-encryption completed.
* Communicated status to customers: investigating increased MFA prompts and login errors; no evidence of compromise; mitigation in place.

Follow-up recovery steps:
* Re-ran re-encryption job with improved retries and reduced concurrency to avoid KMS client/network saturation.
* Verified decrypt success for both key generations across tenants.
* Revoked a small set of long-lived sessions that could not be deterministically mapped for re-encryption (precautionary cleanup).

h1. Where We Got Lucky
* Old-key-abc deletion was scheduled (not immediate), allowing cancellation.
* The hotfix was low-risk and quickly reduced user impact.
* There was no evidence of malicious activity; errors were purely cryptographic/decrypt failures.

h1. What Went Well
* Monitoring quickly correlated auth failures to a specific KMS rotation job.
* Cross-team coordination (Security, Infra, SRE, Auth) was fast; mitigation shipped within ~10 minutes of incident declaration.
* Status communications were timely and accurate.

h1. What Didn’t Go Well
* Rotation automation ordering was unsafe for stateful tokens.
* Re-encryption pipeline lacked “fail closed” gating and strong retries.
* No canary/smoke test was enforced after alias changes.
* Alerting existed for auth failures but not for risky KMS operations (e.g., ScheduleDelete) in close proximity to alias moves.

h1. Action Items
h2. Automation & Safety Gates
# *Add hard gate*: alias move allowed only after re-encryption success verification. (Owner: Olivia Chen; Due: 2026-04-15)
# *Remove ScheduleDelete from rotation run*: require manual approval + minimum retention (e.g., 14 days) for session token keys. (Owner: Ranjit Singh; Due: 2026-04-10)
# *Add post-alias smoke test*: decrypt N representative sessions across tenants and fail rollback on error. (Owner: Noah Patel; Due: 2026-04-18)

h2. Auth-Service Resilience
# *Implement first-class multi-key decrypt*: support decrypt using keyring of active + previous key generation, with automatic sunset. (Owner: Noah Patel; Due: 2026-05-01)
# *Add metrics*: token_decrypt_success_rate by key_id and alias; alert on sudden key_id mismatch. (Owner: Maya Hernandez; Due: 2026-04-20)

h2. Observability & Alerts
# *Alert on KMS ScheduleDelete for production keys*: include key alias context and page on-call if within 24h of rotation. (Owner: Maya Hernandez; Due: 2026-04-12)
# *Audit trail dashboard*: rotation events + re-encryption completion by tenant, including success/failure counts. (Owner: Sarah Kim; Due: 2026-04-25)

h2. Process & Access Control
# *RBAC tightening*: restrict rotation automation permissions to Ops/Security groups; separate role for deletion scheduling. (Owner: Ranjit Singh; Due: 2026-04-22)
# *Runbook update*: add explicit stop conditions (pause rotation if re-encrypt fails >3 retries) and rollback instructions. (Owner: Sarah Kim; Due: 2026-04-08)

h1. Appendix
h2. Key Identifiers (for reference)
* Old key: old-key-abc
* New key: new-key-def
* Alias: session_tokens_v2

h2. Relevant Queries / Signals
KMS audit excerpt observed during incident:
{code}
RotateKey, new-key-def, 2026-03-22T10:01:12Z
UpdateAlias, new-key-def -> session_tokens_v2, 2026-03-22T10:01:15Z
ScheduleDelete, old-key-abc, 2026-03-22T10:03:05Z
{code}

h2. Customer-Facing Status Message (final)
“We identified an issue during a scheduled encryption key rotation that caused increased MFA prompts and intermittent login failures. A mitigation has been deployed and services are recovering. We have no evidence of unauthorized access.”
